title: Validate falsy `AliasGenerator` outputs
author: jiyujie2006
body:
## Summary

Validate falsy invalid values returned by `AliasGenerator` callables before they reach pydantic-core.

The existing check only rejected truthy invalid values, so `0`, `False`, and `[]` could bypass the Python-level `TypeError` and fail later with a lower-level `SchemaError`. Empty strings remain valid aliases, and a returned `None` keeps the existing behavior of leaving the alias unset.

## Checks

- `uv run pytest tests/test_aliases.py::test_alias_generator_with_invalid_callables tests/test_aliases.py::test_alias_gen_with_empty_string tests/test_aliases.py::test_alias_gen_with_empty_string_and_computed_field -q`

title: Allow any type form to be used in `validate_as()`
author: bledden
body:
## Change Summary

`validate_as()` currently rejects Pydantic's own `Annotated` type aliases like `NewPath`, `FilePath`, and `DirectoryPath` at the type-checking level. These are `_AnnotatedAlias` instances (e.g. `Annotated[Path, PathType('new')]`) rather than `type[T]`, so pyright flags them as invalid arguments.

I added an `Any` fallback overload that catches `Annotated` aliases and other type expressions not matched by `type[T]`. The overload resolution order is:

1. `type[_NewOutT]` — preserves precise type inference for concrete types
2. `EllipsisType` — handles the `...` case
3. `Any` — catches everything else (including `Annotated` aliases), returning `_Pipeline[_InT, Any]`

Once PEP 747 (`TypeForm`) lands in type checkers, this fallback can be replaced with a properly typed overload. I added a `TODO PEP 747` comment following the convention used elsewhere in the codebase.

## Related issue number

fix #12845

title: Fix walrus operator precedence in `UrlConstraints.__get_pydantic_core_schema__()`
author: bysiber
body:
## Summary

Fix incorrect walrus operator (`:=`) precedence in `UrlConstraints.__get_pydantic_core_schema__`.

## The Problem

In `pydantic/networks.py`, the current code is:

```python
if annotated_type := schema_to_mutate['type'] not in ('url', 'multi-host-url'):
```

Due to Python's operator precedence, the walrus operator `:=` has lower precedence than `not in`. This means the expression is evaluated as:

```python
annotated_type := (schema_to_mutate['type'] not in ('url', 'multi-host-url'))
```

So `annotated_type` is assigned a boolean (`True`), not the actual schema type string. The error message then reads:

```
'UrlConstraints' cannot annotate 'True'.
```

instead of the intended:

```
'UrlConstraints' cannot annotate 'string'.
```

## The Fix

Add parentheses to ensure the walrus operator captures the type string first:

```python
if (annotated_type := schema_to_mutate['type']) not in ('url', 'multi-host-url'):
```

Now `annotated_type` correctly holds the schema type (e.g. `'string'`, `'int'`), and the error message will display the actual type that was incorrectly annotated.

title: Ensure `__pydantic_private__` is set in `model_construct()` with user-defined `model_post_init()`
author: nightcityblade
body:
Fixes #12813

## Problem

When a model defines a custom `model_post_init` but has no private attributes, `model_construct()` fails to set `__pydantic_private__`, causing `pickle.dumps()` to crash with `AttributeError`.

This happens because:
1. When there are no private attributes, the metaclass does not wrap `model_post_init` with `init_private_attributes`
2. `model_construct` only sets `__pydantic_private__` in the `elif` branch (when `__pydantic_post_init__` is falsy)
3. With a user-defined `model_post_init`, `__pydantic_post_init__` is truthy, so the `elif` branch is skipped
4. The user's `model_post_init` does not set `__pydantic_private__` → attribute never gets set

## Fix

After calling `model_post_init` in `model_construct`, check if `__pydantic_private__` was set. If not, set it to `None`.

## Test

Added `test_model_construct_pickle_with_model_post_init` that reproduces the exact scenario from the issue.

title: Preserve custom docstrings on stdlib dataclasses in JSON schema
author: nightcityblade
body:
Fixes #12812

## Problem

`GenerateJsonSchema` suppresses all `__doc__` from stdlib dataclasses to avoid auto-generated signature docstrings (e.g. `"Foo(x: int = 1)"`) leaking as `description` in JSON schema. However, this also drops user-defined custom docstrings.

## Fix

Distinguish auto-generated docstrings from custom ones by checking if the docstring starts with `f"{cls.__name__}("` — the pattern Python uses for auto-generated dataclass docstrings.

Applied in both code paths:
- `_update_class_schema` (for BaseModel/class schemas)
- `dataclass_schema` (for stdlib dataclass schemas)

## Test

Added `test_stdlib_dataclass_custom_docstring_preserved` verifying:
- Custom docstrings on stdlib dataclasses are preserved as `description`
- Auto-generated docstrings are still suppressed

title: Improve ImportString error when internal imports fail
author: tsembp
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

### What this PR does

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12715.

Improves the error handling of `ImportString` so that internal import failures
(e.g. missing dependencies inside a module) are no longer masked as
`ImportError: No module named ...`.

If the missing module is not the requested import path (or its submodules),
the original `ModuleNotFoundError` is now correctly re-raised.

### Why

Previously, `ImportString` could incorrectly report that a module did not exist,
even when the real issue was a missing internal dependency. This made debugging
harder and hid the true cause of the failure.

### Changes

- Detect whether `ModuleNotFoundError.name` refers to the requested module
- Re-raise internal import errors instead of masking them
- Added tests covering the new behavior

### Tests

- Added new tests in `tests/test_types.py`

title: Make `PydanticUserError` a `RuntimeError` instead of a `TypeError`
author: poliakovva
body:
## Change Summary

This PR updates `PydanticUserError` so that it correctly subclasses `Exception` instead of `TypeError`.

`TypeError` should only be used for errors related to invalid types (e.g., wrong argument type passed to a function). However, `PydanticUserError` is raised for a wide range of incorrect Pydantic usage patterns that are not inherently type-related. Using `Exception` makes its semantics accurate and prevents misleading behavior when catching errors.

### What This PR Does

* Changes the base class of `PydanticUserError` to:

```python
class PydanticUserError(PydanticErrorMixin, Exception):
    """An error raised due to incorrect use of Pydantic."""
```

* Updates all affected tests that previously expected `TypeError` to instead expect `PydanticUserError`
* Ensures all tests pass with the new exception hierarchy

## Related issue number

Fixes #12576

title: Refactor `DecoratorInfos.build()` implementation
author: Viicos
body: ## Change Summary Part of https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/11975. `DecoratorInfos.build()` is currently implemented in a recursive way, and was doing more calls to itself than necessary. For instance, with the following: ```python from pydantic import BaseModel, computed_field class A(BaseModel): @computed_field def f(self) -> int: ... class B: @computed_field def g(self) -> int: ... class C(B): @computed_field def h(self) -> int: ... class D(A, C): pass ``` `DecoratorInfos` was building for the following classes: `B`, `C`, `B`, `A`, with a duplication of `B` because it is also present in the MRO of `c`. For classes that are not "owned" by Pydantic (bare classes, TypedDicts, stdlib dataclasses), we where also mutating these classes (setting the `__pydantic_decorators__` attribute, unwrapping decorators), which is pretty bad as these classes might come from third party libraries and be affected by these mutations. Setting the `__pydantic_decorators__` was done to avoid having to compute the `DecoratorInfos` instance again, so in theory this degrades performance but this is likely not an issue, see section below. --- While working on this, I came across the `Decorator.build()` implementation, computing references with `get_type_ref()` ([known to be slow](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/10863)) for every `build()` call (i.e. every decorator). I added a benchmark in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12538, and can confirm this: In a follow-up PR, I'll try to find a way to optimize the ref computation (presumably we can easily leverage caching).

title: Special case `MISSING` sentinel in `smart_deepcopy()`
author: ornariece
body:
### Summary
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12521.

Deep-copying the experimental `MISSING` sentinel (introduced in 2.12) raises 

> TypeError: Cannot pickle 'Sentinel' object. 

This happens during default resolution in `.model_construct()`, which goes through `smart_deepcopy()`.

This PR special-cases `MISSING` at the top of `smart_deepcopy()` and returns it by identity. That’s all.

### Rationale
- `MISSING` is a singleton sentinel and should be preserved by identity.
- Treating it as such avoids unnecessary copying and the current crash.

### Changes
- `smart_deepcopy()` : early return when obj is `MISSING`.

### Notes
- This PR intentionally keeps changes minimal and does not modify `BaseModel.__deepcopy__()`. If you later decide to route that through `smart_deepcopy()`, this early return will cover that path too.

title: Fix nested model schema deduplication in JSON schema generation
author: marwan-alloreview
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

This fix addresses an issue where nested models with identical Input/Output schemas were not being properly deduplicated, resulting in duplicate schemas like 'User-Input' and 'User-Output' instead of a single 'User' schema.

The root cause was in the _DefinitionsRemapping.from_prioritized_choices() method, where the json_remapping dictionary was only mapping the original key to the remapped key, but not mapping intermediate simplified names.

For example, with alternatives:
  ['__main____Config-Input__1', '__main____Config-Input', 'Config-Input', 'Config']

When 'Config' was chosen as the canonical name, the mapping would only include: '__main____Config-Input__1' -> 'Config'

But after the first iteration, $refs would use 'Config-Input', and without a mapping from 'Config-Input' -> 'Config', subsequent iterations couldn't update those references.

The fix maps ALL alternatives from the remapped index onwards to ensure all intermediate simplification levels are covered.

Related FastAPI discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14288


## Related issue number

Fix #12492

title: Raise a warning when an invalid after model validator function signature is raised
author: Viicos
body:
Reverts https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/11957.

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12413.

The reported flawed signature from the original issue was using the following signature: `(cls, values, info) -> ...`. However, https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/11957 resulted in the much more common (as per this [GH search](https://github.com/search?q=lang%3Apython+%2F%40model_validator%5C%28mode%3D%5B%27%22%5Dafter%5B%22%27%5D%5C%29%5Cs%2Bdef%5Cs.%2B%5C%28cls%2F&type=code)) `(cls, values) -> ...` signature (also not supposed to be accepted) to be confusingly broken (not rejected at build time, but the `values` argument is now the validation info).

According to [this comment](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/pull/2626#issuecomment-3407935823), the high usage of the invalid signature is probably due to V1 root validators changed to _after_ model validators, without changing from a class method to an instance method. As such, I updated the migration guide to mention this change.

title: Remove runtime warning for experimental features
author: Viicos
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Discussed with @davidhewitt, we felt like the runtime warning wasn't really necessary:
- the `experimental` module name already conveys it is experimental
- while we document how to ignore the warning, it might discourage users not familiar with Python that don't know how to do so (and missed the documentation part about it), as they'll see their CI failing because of the warning treated as an error by unittest/pytest.
- if you happen to import a library that makes use of experimental features (and ignored the warning), you won't actually get the warning when importing the `experimental` warning.


I left `PydanticExperimentalWarning` in the code to avoid breaking changes. We could deprecate the warning as it is currently unused, I don't think it is worth the hassle.

title: Add `union_format` parameter to JSON Schema generation
author: Viicos
body: ## Change Summary Fixes (partially) https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7161. A new `union_format` parameter is added to the JSON Schema generation logic, defaulting `'any_of'` (the current behavior): ```python from typing import Annotated from pydantic import BaseModel, Field class Sub(BaseModel): ... class Model(BaseModel): a: int | None b: bool | str c: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=3)] | Annotated[str, Field(min_length=5)] d: list[int] | None e: Sub | None Model.model_json_schema(union_format='primitive_type_array') { │ '$defs': {'Sub': {'properties': {}, 'title': 'Sub', 'type': 'object'}}, │ 'properties': { │ │ 'a': {'title': 'A', 'type': ['integer', 'null']}, │ │ 'b': {'title': 'B', 'type': ['boolean', 'string']}, │ │ 'c': {'anyOf': [{'maxLength': 3, 'type': 'string'}, {'minLength': 5, 'type': 'string'}], 'title': 'C'}, │ │ 'd': {'anyOf': [{'items': {'type': 'integer'}, 'type': 'array'}, {'type': 'null'}], 'title': 'D'}, │ │ 'e': {'anyOf': [{'$ref': '#/$defs/Sub'}, {'type': 'null'}]} │ }, │ 'required': ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'], │ 'title': 'Model', │ 'type': 'object' } ``` It only combines unions into a `type` array when using primitives (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) _and_ when no metadata/constraints are used, otherwise fall backs to `anyOf`. We could also also apply this logic for non-primitives (e.g. arrays), but it can look a bit confusing depending on the tools consuming the JSON Schema. Taking [Swagger UI](https://swagger.io/tools/swagger-ui/) and [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc): | JSON Schema | Swagger UI | Redoc | |--------|--------|--------| |[^1] | | | | [^2] | | | |[^3] | | | | [^4]| | | For this reason, I went with this `'primitive_type_array'` option. If we want to extend this in the future, we could add a new `'type_array'` option that would also use the type array form if non-primitive types are being used (although apart from `"array"` types, I'm not sure this will be really useful as most `"object"` types come from model/dataclasses/typeddicts, which are referenced types and wouldn't be inlined anyway). In the issue thread, it was mentioned to use `oneOf` as well, but I don't think it makes sense to make use of it (even if we are guaranteed that the union members are exclusive, such as ` | None`). `oneOf` means that it successfully validates if _one and only one_ member of the union validates, but this is not how Pydantic performs validation of union types. Depending on the [union mode](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions/#union-modes), union members are validated differently but in all cases there is no constraint that it should only validate against only one member. A new union member could be introduced to do so (and then it would make sense to generate a `oneOf` schema for it), but this wasn't requested so far because the use case is pretty niche. --- I'll also note that FastAPI currently does _not_ support `type` arrays. The fix might be as simple as changing the [`Schema.type` definition](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/6df50d40fe195adc026af169d6ebf298a1c183a5/fastapi/openapi/models.py#L160) from `str | None` to `str | list[str] | None`, but there might be other things to consider. Reported in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/12787. [^1]: `{"type": ["array", "string"], "items": {"type": "string"}}` [^2]: `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}]}` [^3]: `{"type": ["object", "string"], "properties": {"f": {"type": "string"}}}` [^4]: `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "object", "properties": {"f": {"type": "string"}}}]}`
